nodes.name: One-step solid-state reaction for P-Pt₃Co/NC
nodes.procedure: We developed a novel synthesis method via a one-step solid-state reaction to prepare the P-Pt₃Co/NC catalyst (Figure 1a), noting that the eco-friendly phytic acid not only performs the function of the P source but also has a strong cross-link to the metal that easily modulates the P content in the hybrid catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of P-Pt₃Co/NC match face-centered cubic Pt₃Co (JCPDS No. 29-0499) with (111) peaks slightly shifted right indicating lattice shrinkage.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns (Figure 1b) of P-Pt₃Co/NC and Pt₃Co/NC match well with those of standard face-centered cubic Pt₃Co (JCPDS No. 29-0499).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows nanoparticles of 5-13 nm with lattice distances of 2.22 Å and 1.37 Å corresponding to Pt₃Co (111) and (220) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice distances of P-Pt₃Co/NC were measured at 2.22 and 1.37Å respectively, corresponding to the (111) and (220) planes of Pt₃Co.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows alternating brighter Pt and darker Co atoms in crystal framework confirming successful Pt₃Co synthesis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM and EDS images further verify the homogeneous distribution of P, Co, and Pt on the nanoparticles (Figure 1h-l).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS line scan confirms coexistence of Pt, Co, P in individual nanoparticles with homogeneous elemental distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) line scan profile from the purple arrow of the inset of Figure 1g validates the three elements coexist in the individual nanoparticle.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES reveals Pt/Co/P mass percentages of 0.49/0.63/0.68 wt% in P-Pt₃Co/NC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The mass percentages of Pt/Co/P in P-Pt₃Co/NC are respectively 0.49, 0.63, and 0.68 wt % revealed by the inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectrometry (ICP-AES).

nodes.characterization_summary: N₂ physisorption shows specific surface area of 386.8 m²/g for P-Pt₃Co/NC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The specific surface area for P-Pt₃Co/NC is around 386.8 m² g⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f XPS shows metallic Pt⁰ (71.5/74.8 eV), Pt²⁺ (72.2/75.6 eV), Pt-P (73.5/77.1 eV) with ~0.5 eV positive shift vs Pt₃Co/NC indicating charge transfer from Pt to P; Co 2p shows metallic Co (778.6/793.2 eV) and Co²⁺ (781.5/796.3 eV) also positively shifted.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Pt 4f XPS spectra (Figure 2a), the high intensity peaks at 71.5 and 74.8 eV are ascribed to Pt 4f₇/₂ and Pt 4f₅/₂ of metallic Pt⁰ respectively... Notably, the binding energy of Pt 4f in P-Pt₃Co/NC shifts positively (≈0.5 eV) compared to that of Pt₃Co/NC.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge and Pt L₃-edge XANES show positive shifts indicating P doping modifies electronic structure through electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The normalized Pt L₃-edge XANES spectra of P-Pt₃Co/NC in Figure 2d reveals that the absorption edge positively shifts compared with that of Pt₃Co/NC.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Co-P coordination at 1.81 Å with coordination number 2.8; Pt-Pt/Co bonds contract to 2.48 Å confirming P lattice doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform (FT) k³-weighted χ(k)-function of Co EXAFS for P-Pt₃Co/NC in Figure 2e shows a main peak at 1.81 Å, assigned to Co-P coordination.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman under cathodic potential shows Pt-H peak at 2163 cm⁻¹ and P-H peak at 2323.8 cm⁻¹ indicating P acts as proton concentrator enriching protons around adjacent Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 4a, apart from the Pt-H peak at 2163 cm⁻¹, the distinct characteristic peak for P-H under applied potential can be observed at 2323.8 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV determines Cdl=28.8 mF/cm² for P-Pt₃Co/NC vs 14.0 mF/cm² for Pt₃Co/NC indicating abundant active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: P-Pt₃Co/NC demonstrates the highest Cdl value of 28.8 mF cm⁻² compared to those of Pt₃Co/NC (14.0 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows much smaller charge transfer resistance Rct for P-Pt₃Co/NC indicating faster electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The much smaller charge transfer impedance (Rct) for P-Pt₃Co/NC leads to faster electron transfer to boost the hydrogen evolution over the other catalysts (Figure 3e).
